headline: High-risk workspace overlap: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and action-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and uses stdin/stdout plus tool calls; Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP servers. If Devin writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or integrations, AutoGen may ingest it as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction pathway is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo clone
IF Devin writes content that AutoGen later parses as instructions or tool output
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable file-based instruction ingestion for AutoGen
Restrict Devin to read-only on shared artifacts
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization before AutoGen consumes shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad filesystem/network egress; Devin touches source code, docs, issue trackers, and team chat, with Slack/Jira/Notion/GitHub integrations and integration tokens. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive code or secrets can flow from AutoGen into Devin’s cloud-connected outputs, creating exfiltration risk in default configurations.
conditions: IF the same files or secrets are mounted into both agents
IF Devin is allowed to sync workspace contents to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared directories
Use separate credentials per agent
Block Devin integrations on sensitive repos
Run AutoGen in an isolated container
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared files and outbound integrations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. Devin additionally modifies git state and operates with parallel sessions, while AutoGen supports multiple instances with developer-defined shared state. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git history without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Devin commits or rebases while AutoGen is editing the same files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write access with a lock
Disable git writes for one agent
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen produces tool outputs and code execution results that Devin can consume inside its autonomous planner-executor loop. Devin’s browser, shell, and write permissions mean it may act on unverified AutoGen output, turning a mistaken intermediate result into commits, tickets, or messages. The pair therefore supports a default cascade from generated content to downstream action.
conditions: IF Devin treats AutoGen output as authoritative without a verification step
IF AutoGen output is forwarded into Devin’s browser, shell, or integration actions
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Insert a verification step between agents
Limit Devin to draft-only mode
Log and diff all AutoGen outputs before use
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and application data, while Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs through cloud integrations. If regulated or confidential data is placed in shared workspaces, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across vendor-managed cloud services and third-party integrations. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or residency requirements differ across GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review vendor retention settings
Disable unnecessary integrations
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: perform a formal data-flow and residency review
